subject: New law to force tech firms to stop children taking or sharing nude images
posts:
UK demands tech firms block children from sharing nude images, threatening legislation if voluntary device-level controls fall short.
Evidence: 3-month deadline, device scanning, privacy warnings
#Tech #UK

The UK government insists forcing tech giants to build device-level nudity blocks will protect children from online grooming and sextortion.
Stated Judgement: (+0.6, +0.5) — Lesser Good

Mandating device-level nudity blocks forces pervasive surveillance and age verification across all users, threatening adult privacy and encryption under a moral pretext.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.6, -0.7) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
A noble child protection goal is co-opted to justify intrusive device-level surveillance that compromises privacy.

Integrity: Partially Distorted (Hypocrisy: 3.5, Uncertainty z: 2)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- UK Government: FAIL (-0.6, -0.7) — Pushes surveillance under child safety pretext.
- Tech Firms: COND (0.0, 0.0) — Caught between privacy and compliance.
Following a three-month ultimatum, the UK government is moving toward legislation to force tech giants like Apple and Google to block nudity on devices used by minors.

The Bright Side:
Targeting device-level vulnerabilities addresses real risks of sextortion before images are ever shared across platforms.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing WHAT (child safety) with WHO (universal device surveillance). The state substitutes targeted enforcement with blanket monitoring.

Social Physics Analysis:
Ministers run a Smart Selfish Maneuver, leveraging genuine public anxiety over child abuse to mandate architecture that weakens end-to-end encryption for all.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated child protection and universal device surveillance, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil.

The Unavoidable Truth: Protecting children online requires robust technical safeguards against exploitation.

The Unavoidable Lie: Universal device scanning only affects bad actors.

Alethekanon:
Invoking child protection as a blank check for universal device monitoring turns security architecture against its own users.

Awwthekanon:
Every parent wants kids safe from harm, but trading away everyone's digital privacy doesn't keep children safe—it just leaves our digital doors unlocked.

Brothekanon:
Classic government playbook: slap 'think of the children' on a bill so nobody dares question the backdoor surveillance they're sneaking onto your phone.

Spirithekanon:
"Guard your heart above all else, for it determines the course of your life." Proverbs 4:23 FAIL
Trading private boundaries for promised safety surrenders the inner sanctuary.
